units.rationale: The authority boundary is sound, but most of the identity text repeats the base Agent and Runtime contract.
Determining deliverables and constraints is part of ordinary Agent reasoning and should not become a second mandatory workflow.
Acceptance evidence may be useful as addressable state, but the Harness should not require a ledger or prescribe completion classes.
It directs how every substantial action is selected and when branches must close, competing with the model's native planning.
The repeated only, before and immediately rules impose a rigid control policy; the raman case did not show that this improves delivery.
These are useful general habits but largely repeat capabilities already present in the base Agent.
Environment inspection, preserving user work and minimal changes already belong to the base coding Agent instructions.
Verification guidance depends on the task domain and is better supplied by a selected skill or evaluator than a universal Harness.
Research, daemon, recovery and software rules are domain adapters disguised as a universal cognitive procedure.
Progress versus terminal delivery and required artifact existence are I/O protocol properties, not prose that the model must remember.
The cognitive frame should expose optional state affordances rather than summarize a mandatory end-to-end workflow.
The entry task repeats and strengthens the whole procedure, so it directly competes with native task reasoning on every evaluation.
